articles.title: Gianluigi Donnarumma interview: Man City goalkeeper insists club are not in a transition year and backs club to have a great season
articles.summary: Man City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma speaks exclusively to Sky Sports' Sam Blitz about the club's faultless start to the campaign; after a summer of change, City have started on fire; watch Man City vs Sunderland live on Sky Sports this Sunday from 1pm, kick-off 2pm
articles.body:
It's been a few days since the Manchester Derby victory but sat at Man City's training ground, Gianluigi Donnarumma is still basking in the glory.

He's not interested in Erling Haaland's controversial winner - though he's still annoyed Phil Foden was "harshly" sent off earlier in the game - as something else pleased him. A man down, everything going against them - City showed mettle and won.

"I loved my team-mates' performance, it was sublime," he tells Sky Sports . "The capacity to stay in the game and to react to difficult moments - no one can take that away from us.

"We will give everything for this shirt, for this club that gives us so much and offers us so much great support. It has a great history, and we need to give a lot back to it."

Not many had City down to hold a 100 per cent record this season ahead of the upcoming, lengthy international break - especially after losing the core of a successful era in Pep Guardiola, Bernardo Silva, John Stones and Rodri.

City have not been entirely convincing in certain areas - even Donnarumma says there is still lots to learn despite the faultless start to the Enzo Maresca era. But this was meant to be a transition season at City.

"I don't really like the word 'transition.'" he adds. "The club's objective is to win. This team's objective is to win. We'll certainly give everything we can to achieve that.

"We could reach the end of the season having won something, or having won nothing. But what's important is having a winning mentality, going out there and trying to win everything we possibly can."

Part of that winning mentality is being driven by Donnarumma - who is part of a newly-formed leadership group that replaced the likes of Bernardo, Stones and Rodri.

Donnarumma sits alongside Ruben Dias in the leadership pecking order, along with Haaland and Marc Guehi. All four players have one thing in common: they all have won trophies both at City and at other clubs in their careers.

So as the likes of Ayyoub Bouaddi, Elliot Anderson and Iliman Ndiaye settle into their new team - tasked with making an immediate impact in a non-transition year - the leadership quartet are there to drive the standards.

"We've changed a few players. A few new ones have arrived," says Donnarumma. "They're all top players who are used to playing on the biggest stages, dealing with certain situations, and playing in the Premier League.

"It's not easy at the beginning when you move to a new club, a new organisation, a new city. But they're adapting well, and we're making them feel comfortable.

"The players who were already here are helping them a lot. I think we're going to have a great season.

"The objective is to get to the end and compete for everything there is to compete for - in addition to the Premier League, there's the Champions League and the two domestic cups."

It's a clear warning from City that anything is possible when it comes to this team. But when it comes to Donnarumma's aim of challenging for the Premier League and the Champions League, one team stands in the way: Arsenal.

Mikel Arteta's side also started the season with four straight league wins (before their defeat to Brighton) - and have the added recent psychological boost of pipping City to the Premier League post last May.

The recent Guardiola documentary showed down and disappointed scenes from City players as they slipped up at Bournemouth to hand the Gunners the title. Donnarumma - who had won the league title in each of the previous five seasons before last term - was one of them.

"It's difficult, but that's football, that's life. You're not on your own," he says about that disappointment. "There are other strong teams, especially in the Premier League.

"It's not that if you don't win there isn't disappointment - of course there is - but it can happen because there are other teams as well, just like in the Champions League.

"It's important to go into every game trying to win it. Certainly, our objective will be to win, but there are other teams too.

"You have to compete, you have to work, and you have to do everything possible because the history of this club demands it."

Will it be City and Arsenal again competing at the top come May? "I don't know. We're only four games into the season," says the Italian goalkeeper.

But the stall has been set out. "Our focus right now has to be on working and trying to win every game. That has to be our objective.

"Whether we achieve it in the end or not, only time will tell."

Watch Man City vs Sunderland in the Premier League live on Sky Sports' Super Sunday from 1pm, kick-off 2pm.

articles.body:
Cesar Menotti e Fabiano se apresentam na 1ª Expo Rural de Maricá, no Rio. — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

A 1ª Expo Rural de Maricá , na Região Metropolitana do Rio, movimenta o fim de semana com entrada gratuita e shows sertanejos de Zé Felipe e da dupla César Menotti & Fabiano no Parque de Exposições da cidade, no bairro Espraiado.

O evento, que segue até 27 de setembro, reúne atrações voltadas ao setor agropecuário, feira agrícola, exposição de animais, praça de alimentação e a disputa do Rodeio Classificatório para Barretos.

A Prefeitura de Maricá organizou um esquema especial de transporte público, com linhas de ônibus que ligam os bairros do entorno à região do evento.

Também foi planejado um esquema de segurança para a circulação e o acesso ao espaço, que inclui a proibição de coolers, guarda-chuvas, cadeiras de praia, utensílios de vidro, objetos perfurocortantes e alimentos ou bebidas em lata.

articles.body: LaLiga 26-27 llega este domingo con cinco partidos tremendamente interesantes. El Getafe se enfrenta al Málaga a las 14:00. Más tarde, a las 16:15, llega el gran derbi entre el Atlético de Madrid y el Real Madrid. A las 18:30 se disputan a la vez el Villarreal-Levante y el Deportivo-Betis. Y cierra la jornada el Valencia vs Real Sociedad, a las 21:00. Dentro de las apuestas deportivas, Betfair paga a 1.44 que el encuentro tenga menos de tres goles. Betfair paga a 1.38 que ambos equipos marquen en el derbi madrileño. Pronóstico 3: Gana el Villarreal El conjunto de Marcelino llega lanzado tras golear 3-1 en Málaga, su mejor resultado a domicilio de la temporada, mientras que el Levante arrastra dudas defensivas importantes y todavía no ha podido disputar su partido de la jornada anterior por la suspensión ante el Athletic debido a la lluvia. Ambos conjuntos han demostrado capacidad para ver puerta en la mayoría de sus salidas esta temporada. Betfair paga a 1.66 que ambos equipos marquen. Pronóstico 5: -2.5 goles totales El Valencia rescató una victoria de mérito por 0-1 en Mendizorroza gracias a un gol en el descuento de Luis Rioja, un resultado ajustado y de poca producción ofensiva, mientras que la Real Sociedad empató sin goles ante el Celta en su última salida. articles.title: St Mirren 0-3 Dundee United: Jim Goodwin enjoys winning return to the dugout
articles.summary: Report as Dundee United mark Jim Goodwin’s return to the dugout with a commanding 3-0 win at St Mirren as Jesse Randall, Lyall Cameron and Kevin Ciubotaru strike in the first half.
articles.body:
All three goals - from Jesse Randall, Lyall Cameron and Kevin Ciubotaru - came in the first half with United also benefiting from the decision to downgrade Daniel Bennie's red card to a yellow.

It was the perfect matchday return for Goodwin, following a recent health scare, against his former club, who slumped to a third league defeat in a row after failing to register a shot on target.

St Mirren made three changes from the side beaten by Rangers in their previous outing. In came Eseosa Sule, Paul Nsio and Killian Phillips, with Nikolas Agrafiotis, Chris Mochrie and Louis Jackson dropping out.

United also made three switches to the line-up. There were starting berths for Zidane Iqbal, Randall and Idjessi Metsoko, while Pan Camara, Mehdi Merghem and Zac Sapsford all made way.

It took United just six minutes to take the lead. Bennie played in Randall and, as Calvin Ramsay and goalkeeper Jacob Chapman hesitated, the forward rounded the goalkeeper to finish.

The home side tried to respond quickly but Fraser Taylor's shot sailed high over the stand and, instead, it was United who doubled their lead after 12 minutes. Metsoko picked out Cameron, who cut in from the left wing and his low shot beat Chapman.

Saints looked to have been handed a way back into the contest when they were awarded a penalty for a foul by Bert Esselink on Phillips, but after a long VAR check the decision was overturned due to offside in the build-up.

The home side were struggling to get into any sort of rhythm although Nsio came close with a powerful shot that struck the top of the crossbar and went over.

United looked like they were set to be reduced to 10 men late in the first half when Bennie made a crude tackle on Ryan Carr, but after a VAR check the sanction was reduced from red card to yellow.

The visitors took advantage of that let-off by scoring a third goal just before the break. Randall played in Ciubotaru and he fired his effort past Chapman.

It was United who still looked more likely after the turnaround and Dylan Tait was only denied a fourth by a strong Chapman save.

The visitors were then denied by the offside side flag after Lachlan Rose had slid Randall's cross beyond the goalkeeper.

articles.title: Quique: "Quien nos dijera que íbamos a llegar al primer parón con 11 puntos igual no se lo creía"
articles.standfirst: El técnico valoró de forma positiva el punto en San Mamés
articles.summary: El técnico valoró de forma positiva el punto en San Mamés
articles.body: Quique Sánchez Flores compareció ante los medios de comunicación para hacer un balance del empate en San Mamés. Valoración: "Puntuar aquí siempre es complicado. Ves el estadio desde fuera y te das cuenta de que es muy complicado sumar puntos. Nosotros tenemos grandes sensaciones porque después de un gran arranque, habíamos perdido dos partidos consecutivos y teníamos algo de tristeza. En Bilbao hemos estado muy bien y conseguimos recuperar las buenas sensaciones". Arranque de Liga: "Quien nos dijera que íbamos a llegar al primer parón con 11 puntos igual no se lo creía. Hemos hecho un buen arranque de temporada y la confianza ha vuelto. En esta plantilla todos cuentan y hoy hemos hecho cambios con respecto a los últimos partidos. Las cosas nos han salido bien, ha habido momentos en los que el rival nos ha metido demasiado en el bloque bajo, pero hemos sido capaces de mantener el resultado con solvencia. Ha salido bien el plan que habíamos previsto". Nivel defensivo: "Hemos hecho el trabajo defensivo que debíamos hacer. Nos hubiese gustado tener más salida. Los dos últimos partidos se nos habían ido por problemas defensivos y hoy hemos conseguido recuperar las buenas sensaciones. Los chicos han estado muy preparados para los duelos y para cuidar todos los detalles". Athletic: "La ocasión más peligrosa ha sido el penalti. El equipo ha estado muy cómodo, ha sido contundente y en los duelos hemos estados sólidos. Hemos puesto el partido muy difícil a jugadores como Nico y Sancet. Estamos contentos por volver a sumar, en un derbi y ante un equipo como el Athletic. Ellos son muy fuertes físicamente, tienen un diseño extraordinario".

articles.title: Simeone, una lista para el derbi sin Barrios ni Sorloth
articles.standfirst: Los dos son las únicas bajas para el encuentro ante el Real Madrid
articles.summary: Los dos son las únicas bajas para el encuentro ante el Real Madrid
articles.body: Como era de esperar, el Atlético ha dado la lista de convocados con dos grandes ausencias. Ni Barrios ni Sorloth han podido llegar a tiempo y no están en la convocatoria para medirse mañana al Real Madrid en el Metropolitano. Se tratan de dos bajas importantes, en especial la del canterano, ya el gran líder de una medular que no puede manejar tanto como le gustaría por sus recurrentes lesiones musculares. La última, de hecho, le dejará sin un nuevo derbi. En cualquier caso, llega al parón y en el Atlético no han querido correr riesgos con ambos futbolistas, que estarán listos para después de las tres semanas sin Liga. Están en la convocatoria Esquivel, habitual tercer portero, Domínguez y Castillo, así como un Dani Martínez que pese a llevar el dorsal 30 es jugador del primer equipo.

articles.title: Pau comanda a España a las semifinales
articles.standfirst: Con un gol de la dorsal 20, las de David Aznar vencen a Brasil y pasan de ronda
articles.summary: Con un gol de la dorsal 20, las de David Aznar vencen a Brasil y pasan de ronda
articles.body: El equipo de David Aznar no quería cambiar el plan de juego que ha mantenido todo el torneo. Dominar con el balón y asediar hasta marcar. Y volvieron a conseguirlo, siendo superiores a Brasil, sabiendo aguantar y gracias al gol de Pau Comendador, la selección española se clasifica para las semifinales del Mundial. Muchos cambios los que realizó el técnico español en el XI respecto a los octavos. Entraron Pau, Cerrato, Librán, Segura y Peñalvo. La primera ocasión la tuvo Brasil, en un disparo lejano de Kaylane de volea que Laia tuvo que detener en dos tiempos. Sin embargo, España se mantuvo fiel al fútbol que ha practicado durante todo el torneo, ejerciendo el papel dominante. Las bandas fueron claves para el triunfo. Noe Bejarano y Noa Jiménez, doblando cada vez que podían, estaban siendo un auténtico dolor de cabeza. Pero el gol vino con las jugadoras más adelantadas. Rosalía, que cada vez que cogía el balón inventaba algo, alcanzó la línea de fondo y puso el pase atrás. Allí estaba Pau Comendador, que de primeras remató. A punto estuvo de sacarlo Thaynara cuando se dirigía a la meta, pero acabó entrando. El dominio español era cada vez más evidente ante una Brasil que parecía sufrir la fatiga de la prórroga contra Estados Unidos. Noe Bejarano tuvo que salir sustituida en el descanso tras hacerse daño en los minutos finales de la primera parte. El cuadro sudamericano salió al ataque la segunda mitad buscando la igualada desde que pitó la colegiada. Las brasileñas incomodaron más a las españolas que en la primera parte, aunque no conseguían generar un gran peligro a la meta de Laia. Celia Segura tuvo en sus pies el segundo para poner tierra de por medio. Acabó una buena contra desde la frontal, pero Thais primero y el palo después, evitaron el gol. Brasil insistía, pero no conseguía la igualada. España, que pasó de dominar a resistir, estaba consiguiendo su objetivo. El tiempo pasaba. Agote pudo marcar el segundo en el descuento, pero su disparo se estrelló en el palo tras tocar una rival. Finalmente, Brasil se quedó a cero y España con un solitario gol de Pau Comendador pasó a las semifinales donde nos esperaba Italia.

articles.title: El Eibar le hace el 'Lío' al Eldense
articles.standfirst: Enlaza su quinta victoria con mucho sufrimiento
articles.summary: Consigue su quinta victoria seguida con mucho sufrimiento
articles.body: El primer encuentro de la Era Messi no pudo acabar con un triunfo del Eldense, equipo que trato muy bien el balón y que dominó a un Eibar que, al final, ganó con mucho sufrimiento para enlazar su quinta victoria seguida. El primer tiempo transitó con alternancia en el juego, si bien el Eibar con la idea clara de robar y buscar la banda de Adu Ares quien, en los primeros minutos, fue un quebradero de cabeza intentaba golpear. El Eldense buscaba con la maestría de Fidel filtrar una y otra vez esféricos en busca de consumar en área visitante peligro. Los armeros no dudaron en morder la salida de juego del Eldense y, de una presión sobre Roberto López, el robo de balón lo transformó Magunazelaia en el 0-1. Tras la reanudación, el Eldense salió súper enchufado, con presión muy alta y se apuntó al acoso y derribo, pero los armeros rechazaban todos los balones. El Eibar sufría con esa presión de los del debutante Calleja, aunque aprovechó una contra para marcar el 0-2: Iván Gil la engatilló como un misil y tras tocar en el larguero botaba dentro. Revisión del VAR y gol. Un golpe duro para un dominador Eldense que era consciente que remontar al Eibar es una misión demasiado complicada. Los vascos seguían sin prisa atrás ante el empuje local. La tuvo Manu Nieto y Olabarrieta. Cuesta arriba, el Eldense fue capaz de meterse en el encuentro cuando Justin Smith conectó en la frontal un ajustado golpeo que entró al lado de la cepa del poste. Quiso creer el Eldense y apretó más ante el muro de hormigón que construyeron los armeros, en él cual se estrellaron una y otra vez los pupilos de Javi Calleja.

articles.title: 12 goles en contra en dos partidos: "Tenemos una sensación de mierda"
articles.standfirst: El Racing recibió siete tantos en el encuentro ante el Barcelona y cinco contra el Celta. "Es época de hacer autocrítica", dice Mantilla
articles.summary: El Racing recibió siete tantos en el encuentro ante el Barcelona y cinco contra el Celta. "Es época de hacer autocrítica", dice Mantilla
articles.body: El Racing ha sufrido dos goleadas consecutivas ante el Barcelona (7-2) y esta tarde contra el Celta (5-0). Dos partidos que dejan muy tocado al conjunto cántabro en apenas cuatro días. Los hombres de José Alberto han recibido 12 goles en estos dos encuentros, sumando ya 21 en contra en las siete primeras jornadas. La apuesta futbolística del Racing, muy ofensiva en Segunda división, la ha trasladado el entrenador a la máxima categoría y, de momento, se está convirtiendo en una sangría goleadora. El conjunto cántabro está muy serio como local, donde no ha perdido y suma los siete puntos que lleva en su casillero. Pero a domicilio no es igual: cuatro partidos disputados, cuatro derrotas, dos de ellas ante Barcelona y Celta con goleada en contra. A todo esto hay que sumar que Agirrezabala ha sido de los mejores en estas últimas derrotas, por lo que todavía podría haber sido peor. "Somos mayorcitos para mirarnos el ombligo con la semana que hemos hecho. Es época de hacer autocrítica. Son demasiados goles. Tenemos una sensación de mierda, porque somos un muy buen equipo y no merecemos estos goles. Tenemos que ser mucho más intensos en todos los duelos, tener más unión, tener más equipo y sacaremos los resultados porque confío en este equipo", aseguraba Mantilla, jugador del Racing, en Movistar LaLiga. De la misma opinión era el técnico José Alberto. "Son dos resultados muy dolorosos, nos hacen daño. Tenemos que hacer una reflexión profunda de lo que estamos haciendo y ser conscientes de que fuera de casa, con lo que estamos haciendo, no nos da", dijo en Movistar LaLiga.

articles.title: Moriba: “Este es el Celta que extrañábamos”
articles.standfirst: El mediocampista firmó un partido notable ante el Racing, con gol incluido
articles.summary: El mediocampista firmó un partido notable ante el Racing, con gol incluido
articles.body: IIaix Moriba hizo su primer gol de la temporada y firmó un partido notable. El mediocampista se refería a su tanto en los micrófonos de Movistar: “Hay muchas veces que entra y muchas veces que no. Hoy, gracias a Dios, ha podido entrar y ayudar para sumar los tres puntos". Sobre la actuación de su equipo hasta el penalti, dijo: "Está a la vista que hemos empezado un poco mal y, aunque no quieras, la confianza cuenta y hay dudas. Puede ser que hayamos empezado con dudas y esta victoria nos viene bien para después del parón ser nosotros mismos e ir a por los objetivos que teníamos”. Volvió el equipo que él quería: “El Celta que extrañábamos. A veces hay partidos que se complican más, a veces salen las cosas y otras no y hoy salió. A disfrutarlo para que nos ayude”. Cree que deben seguir en la misma línea: “Las cosas no hay por qué cambiarlas, ya que llevamos mucho tiempo haciendo un buen trabajo, aunque en los partidos no se veía. Es seguir trabajando como lo veníamos haciendo y que esto nos ayude para tener confianza y ser nosotros mismos".

articles.title: Aaron McLean's EFL takeaways including Wrexham, Bradford City and Gillingham
articles.summary: BBC Final Score pundit Aaron McLean looks at the weekend's talking points in the EFL, including Wrexham, QPR and Bradford City.
articles.body:
Former Peterborough United and Hull City striker - and Final Score pundit - Aaron McLean gives his five takeaways following Saturday's action in the Championship, League One and League Two.

Can Wrexham turn statement wins into something more consistent?

Wrexham ended Southampton's five-match unbeaten run by winning 2-1 to claim their first home win of the season. Expectations remain high in north Wales, such is the public profile of the club and the investment into the squad but they have been an inconsistent prospect so far this campaign.

McLean: "Do I think Wrexham are a candidate for automatic promotion? Probably not, but that win against Southampton will give them huge confidence.

"That was only their second win of the season and they have probably come under pressure for the first time. Last season they were outstanding and, personally I think overachieved and the level of expectation has risen as a result but the team has not quite lived up to it.

"To beat Southampton, as one of the in-form teams in the division, will do them and Phil Parkinson no end of good.

"They need to be more clinical. You look at West Ham – 22 goals; Middlesbrough – 16 goals. You look at the top end of the pitch and they have the players who can find ways to kill games off.

"Wrexham have drawn four games because they have not been able to kill games off but, if they are in the shake-up, I would not bet against their owners in January saying, 'right, let's go and get the missing piece of the puzzle'."

Wrexham earn last-gasp victory over Southampton

Given Preston's predicament towards the foot of the Championship, QPR may well feel their 2-2 draw was two points dropped but they fought back from 2-0 down and Dennis Cirkin's red card in the 15th minute to claim a draw at Loftus Road. Julien Stephan's R's are fifth in the Championship table and remain firmly in the promotion mix.

McLean: "I have been so impressed with QPR. I think they have been outstanding and they can genuinely stay around the play-off places.

"Glen Kamara in the middle of the park is an outstanding player who I think could play in the Premier League. Their recruitment has been first class.

"With the squad they have got, I really like the look of them this season. For a few years they have probably spent money in the wrong places but they have addressed that and can look forward to having a really competitive season.

"Julien Stephan has done a hugely impressive job – the 7-1 defeat to Coventry [at the start of last season] has been the making of them – and I am really looking forward to seeing them over the rest of the season."

QPR score last-minute equaliser against Preston

Bradford City's 58-year wait for a win over Luton Town has enabled them to usurp Sheffield Wednesday at the top of League One. The Bantams have only scored seven goals in seven games but have conceded just four - the joint-best defensive record in the EFL. Predictably, given his history at Deepdale as a player, Graham Alexander has been linked with the vacancy at Preston North End.

McLean: "Bradford are a massive club, you only have to listen to the noise they make at Valley Parade and the support they get and Graham Alexander is an outstanding manager who is at the right club for him to continue progressing.

"This season, their bouncebackability has stood out. They won their first two games, then after back-to-back defeats you are looking at them and thinking, 'oh was it just a good start' but then they go and win three in a row, so even in adversity they can bounce back and respond in the right way.

"Is their lack of goals sustainable for a promotion challenge? No, probably not but, at the moment, it hasn't needed to be because they have been so good defensively and so hard to beat.

"And that's from front to back and when they do get their noses in front, they know how to see games out.

"I expect their conversion rate to improve and Bobby Pointon is a fantastic young striker who I have tipped to be one of the best strikers in the division over the next few seasons."

Slow and steady progress for Bromley in League One

Bromley ended Huddersfield Town's unbeaten start to the season with a 2-1 victory at the Copperjax Community Stadium - their first since the opening day of the 2026-27 season. It has been a challenging first few weeks for the club in the third tier for the first time in their history, losing three games in a row and conceding 14 goals in the process but Andy Woodman's squad have shown their resilience and quality to come through that period.

McLean: "For Bromley, it is sometimes easy to lose sight of where they have come from, how quickly they have got here, and the jump that exists between League Two and the top end of League One. It is really, really tough for newly-promoted teams and it is going to take time to adapt.

"To come out winners against Huddersfield who were the form team in the division will do them the world of good.

"It shows they have the character and the belief in the dressing room that even on the back of a run of defeats they can go again, and compete and get positive results against teams of the size of Huddersfield.

"Andy Woodman will be absolutely delighted. For a club of Bromley's size and where they have been, consolidation in League One will surely be the goal this season and these three points will go a long way to helping achieve that."

In a wide open League Two, is this the season the Gills get it right?

Since dropping down to League Two four years ago, Gillingham have never finished higher than 12th, a poor return for a club of their size and reputation. But their eye-catching 3-0 win over Bristol Rovers means they are now the form side in the division with three wins and three draws over their past six and have moved up to fourth with signs pointing towards something stirring within Gareth Ainsworth's squad.

McLean: "I spoke to Gareth Ainsworth in the summer and he admitted he got it wrong last season. They perhaps overachieved a bit at the start and that created a false impression of where they were as a squad.

"Gareth has ripped up the script a bit and they have looked really really positive and are playing their way into form.

"He is huge on the psychological aspect of management and players 'emptying the tank' and to play for Gareth Ainsworth you have to buy into that.

"When you look at their performances and the way they are achieving these results it looks like another squad of players who have bought into his ideas.

"You look at his Wycombe sides, you don't have to be the biggest club in the division as long as everyone is pulling in the right direction then you can be successful."

Aaron McLean was speaking to BBC Sport England's James Piercy

articles.body: José Alberto, que lamentó la abultada derrota, reconocía que el Racing empezó bien el partido. "El resultado es muy duro para nosotros, sobre todo porque creo hemos estado bien en el comienzo y hasta el segundo gol. Luego hemos perdido el control", aseguraba tras el encuentro. El técnico asturiano tiene claro que los dos últimos resultados han sido mazazo: "La semana es dura y dolorosa para todos nosotros, el equipo tiene que ser más competitivo, ofrecer una mejor cara y adaptarnos a la categoría". Sobre las dos goleadas, dijo en Movistar: "Son dos resultados muy dolorosos, nos hacen daño. Tenemos que hacer una reflexión profunda de lo que estamos haciendo y ser conscientes de que fuera de casa, con lo que estamos haciendo, no nos da". José Alberto, por otro lado, alababa el partido de su rival: "El Celta es un equipo con jugadores mucho más asentados en la categoría y lo que han hecho es oler sangre y reventarnos". Para el entrenador racinguista, el parón será positivo: "Creo que nos va a venir bien para conjuntarnos, porque lo hemos tenido que hacer durante la competición. Quiero que contra el Valencia seamos el equipo que quiero ver".

articles.title: Ohio State closes out first-half rout of Kent State with Hail Mary touchdown
articles.summary: With 3 seconds left in the first half, Julian Sayin found Brandon Inniss in a crowded end zone on the way to the Buckeyes' dominant 59-3 win.
articles.body:
No. 6 Ohio State shook off last week's tough loss to Texas by taking care of business against Kent State. In a 59-3 rout over the Golden Flashes, the Buckeyes took a 35-0 lead at halftime with a big Hail Mary touchdown in the final seconds of the first half.

After OSU's defense forced Kent State to turn the ball over on downs with less than 30 seconds remaining, the Buckeyes and starting quarterback Julian Sayin quickly went to work. Thanks to a roughing-the-passer call and a 15-yard pass to Jeremiah Smith, OSU ended up just past midfield with three seconds left on the clock.

Kent State's defense put pressure on Sayin after the snap, leading the quarterback to scramble into space. From there, he launched the ball toward the end zone; Inniss was there to pull down the ball, beating five Kent State defenders to give the Buckeyes another touchdown.

The score, as the clock hit zero, marked the Buckeyes' fifth touchdown of the first half. Ohio State added another touchdown early in the second half, taking advantage of a forced fumble to bring the score to 42-0.

With the game well in hand, head coach Ryan Day opted to pull many of his starters. Smith, who had broken the school's career receiving yards record earlier in the game, ended up on the bench shortly after halftime; Sayin joined him later in the third quarter.

With the second-stringers in, Ohio State wasn't quite as productive on offense, but still managed to score later in the half. Freshman QB Luke Fahey got picked off by Kent State in the end zone before the end of the third quarter, but made up for it with a 75-yard touchdown pass to Chris Henry Jr. on the Buckeyes' next drive.

The eight touchdowns in all gave OSU a 59-3 win , with Kent State breaking up the shutout with a field goal late in the fourth quarter. Still, the Buckeyes were able to cap off their non-conference schedule with a definitive victory.

Even against a lesser opponent, Ohio State's stats spoke for themselves: The Buckeyes racked up 527 total yards, including 382 passing yards from Sayin and Fahey, while allowing just 134 total yards from the Golden Flashes.

articles.title: Justice Haynes scores 3 TDs in 44-11 Georgia Tech win over Mercer
articles.summary: Georgia Tech (1-2) followed up home defeats to Colorado and Tennessee with an uneven performance for most of the first half, but pulled away thanks to Haynes...
articles.body:
Justice Haynes rushed for 141 yards on 22 carries with three touchdowns — two rushing, one receiving — leading Georgia Tech to its first victory of the season, 44-11 over Mercer at Bobby Dodd Stadium.

Georgia Tech (1-2) followed up home defeats to Colorado and Tennessee with an uneven performance for most of the first half, but pulled away thanks to Haynes and quarterback Alberto Mendoza .

"I do think we've improved each week," Georgia Tech head coach Brent Key said. "That being said, it was a pretty low starting point, though."

The Yellow Jackets scored 10 points in the final two minutes before the break to take a 24-3 lead and added three more second-half touchdowns. Mendoza completed 15 of 21 passes for a season-high 249 yards, finding Javien Plummer and Debron Gatling for scoring strikes from 37 and 33 yards out.

"The first half wasn't our standard," Mendoza said. "I think we could clean a lot of those things up, and at halftime we addressed a lot of those things."

Zahmari Palode-Gary led Mercer (2-2) with 71 rushing yards on 15 carries.

Georgia Tech did not force a turnover in either of its first two games, but finally found two Saturday. Taje McCoy forced an early fumble with pressure off the edge and freshman Christian Speakman fell on the loose ball. Another freshman, linebacker C.J. Gamble, grabbed Georgia Tech's first interception of the season with an alert play on a low throw.

"I feel like it's been a constant progression just being able to put plays together on defense," McCoy said. "It's just doing my job and making the plays I'm supposed to make, and it's finally starting to show."

The Yellow Jackets won the turnover battle 2-0, and cashed both in for touchdowns.

Stopping the run was a major concern for the Yellow Jackets heading into Saturday after giving up 299 yards on the ground against Tennessee, and the question is still in the fold after another poor performance. Mercer rushed for 188 yards on 46 attempts, and had six different run plays go for at least 11 yards.

Mercer: The Bears made a quarterback change late in the second quarter. JP Pickles took over and led the Bears on two field goal drives, accounting for 53 rushing yards with an efficient 7-of-11 passing clip for 82 yards.

Georgia Tech: The Yellow Jackets finally got what they were looking for from their star transfer, Haynes. After just 145 total rushing yards and no plays over 20 yards in the first two games, the former Michigan back and projected focal point of Georgia Tech's offense was explosive in open space, highlighted by his 31-yard touchdown run in the third quarter.

Mercer: Steps back into Championship Subdivision play at Abilene Christian next Saturday.

Georgia Tech: Opens its Atlantic Coast Conference slate at Stanford next Saturday.

articles.title: Liverpool Are In Talks With The Agent Of This Ligue 1 Midfielder: What Will He Bring To Anfield?
articles.summary: In a recent interview with Football Insider, former Manchester United scout Mick Brown mentioned that Liverpool are in talks with the agent of Monaco midfiel...
articles.body:
In a recent interview with Football Insider , former Manchester United scout Mick Brown mentioned that Liverpool are in talks with the agent of Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara . Brown said

"Lamine Camara is a name that has been discussed behind the scenes.

"Liverpool will be keeping an eye on how he gets on for Monaco, but there is definitely a deal to be done as we saw when he nearly joined Chelsea .

"His agent has been very outspoken about trying to get him a move, so I expect Liverpool will have held talks with him about the possibility of signing him in January.

"They'll know his demands, they'll have done their homework about his attitude and how he might fit into the squad, because it's important they don't just rush into it.

"It's something Liverpool have been working on, they're doing their due dilligence, and there is a real possibility they could do a deal."

Camara's Impressive Rise In French Football

Camara enjoyed a good run of form at the French club after he put in a series of influential displays for them in the middle of the park. The French talent banged in three goals and earned four assists in 31 matches for Monaco last season across all fronts.

The 22-year-old is currently one of the best central midfielders in Ligue 1. Hence, it is no wonder that the Reds are hoping to land him in this transfer window.

DUBLIN, IRELAND – JUNE 06: Lamine Camara Mamadou of Senegal warms up prior to the international friendly match between Republic of Ireland and Senegal at Aviva Stadium on June 06, 2025 in Dublin, Ireland. (Photo by Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)

Camara is a solid tackler of the ball and can read the danger well to earn possession back for his team inside his half. He usually puts his foot through the ball when needed and is a tidy passer as well from midfield.

The French sensation can even chip in by scoring and creating his fair share of goals from midfield. Camara is primarily a box-to-box midfielder but can also serve as a defensive midfielder if asked to do so. However, there are some concerns over whether he can cope with the physical side and high intensity of the Premier League if the Reds manage to bring him on board next year.

We can expect Camara to bring more quality and depth to Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola's midfield. He has what it takes to fight for a regular first-team spot at the Merseyside club in the coming years.

At 22, Camara has the potential to be a world-class player in English football someday. Thus, the Reds should focus on getting him on board this January or next summer.

articles.title: Madrid Daily: La Fábrica wins at the Bernabéu as derby preparations conclude
articles.summary: Mbappé leaves Nike for On, Simeone praises Mourinho, and Víctor Muñoz reflects on his time at Madrid.
articles.body:
Real Madrid celebrated a title at the Bernabéu on Saturday as Álvaro López's youngsters beat Santiago Wanderers to win the Under-20 Intercontinental Cup, completing a four-trophy haul for La Fábrica. The first team, meanwhile, wrapped up preparations for Sunday's derby at the Metropolitano, with fitness updates and selection decisions taking shape on both sides of the rivalry. Away from the pitch, Kylian Mbappé 's partnership with On marks a new commercial chapter, while Víctor Muñoz reflects on the experiences that shaped his development at Madrid.

Real Madrid won their first Under-20 Intercontinental Cup on Saturday, beating Santiago Wanderers 3–1 at the Santiago Bernabéu. The victory made Madrid the first Spanish club to lift the trophy and completed a four-title haul in 2026 for Álvaro López's team, following their successes in the league, Copa de Campeones and UEFA Youth League.

Dani Yáñez opened the scoring with a direct free kick in the 29th minute, shortly after Wanderers defender Alexander Dubó was sent off for a challenge on him. Madrid controlled much of the first half but were brought back level four minutes after the restart, when Christian Silva scored for the visitors.

The decisive intervention came from substitute Fran Santamaría, who converted Jesús Fortea's low cross in the 81st minute. Wanderers subsequently lost Cristopher Valenzuela and Nicolás Carvacho to red cards, finishing with eight players. Although Yáñez had a stoppage-time penalty saved, Roberto Martín added Madrid's third in the 99th minute, again from a Fortea assist.

The match also established a new attendance record for the competition, with 52,117 spectators at the Bernabéu. That surpassed the 45,656 who attended Flamengo's meeting with Barcelona at the Maracanã in 2025, an increase of 6,461. This was the first edition of the Under-20 Intercontinental Cup staged in Europe.

Álvaro López: "This is a historic generation"

For López, winning at the Bernabéu carried a significance beyond the trophy itself. Speaking after the match, the coach recalled his childhood connection to the stadium.

"Well, imagine… For me, a Real Madrid fan like myself, a member since birth, from the Barrio del Pilar… My grandfather brought me to the Bernabéu from the time I was born, I experienced historic nights. From the stadium, from home. And well, we're incredibly happy and grateful. Proud to be able to make history."

Asked about the difficulty of the final, López said:

"Real Madrid doesn't just play in finals, they win them. And that's exactly what happened. It was a tough match, they made it very difficult for us, but the important thing was to enjoy it. We'll take this with us to cherish, something unforgettable."

He also acknowledged the support the team received from the club and its supporters.

"We have spoken with the president, and he congratulated us. We are very grateful to everyone, to the club, to Mourinho… Feeling the support of the fans… This is something we will cherish forever."

López reserved particular praise for the players and what they have achieved together.

"This is a historic generation. They've won the second Youth League title and the first Under-20 Intercontinental Cup. It's a legacy that will stand. They're nearing the end of their time here, we have a fantastic team, and we're incredibly proud. They embody the values of Real Madrid. This belongs to them. And now, back to work, as they always do."

Captain Carlos Díez, who joined López for the post-match press conference, emphasized the years of shared work behind the success.

"I'm very happy. Winning this title with teammates I've known for six or seven years… I'm very proud and happy. We've worked day after day to achieve this."

Madrid finish derby preparations with three players still recovering

Real Madrid completed their final training session before Sunday's derby against Atlético Madrid at the Metropolitano. The match, corresponding to the seventh round of LaLiga, kicks off on September 20 at 4:15 p.m. Madrid time.

Saturday's session began with warm-up exercises and rondos before moving into tactical work, pressing and possession drills. The players finished with small-sided games and shooting practice. Ferland Mendy , Éder Militão and Rodrygo continued their recovery programs and remain unavailable for the derby.

Aurélien Tchouaméni, meanwhile, is fully reintegrated into the group after returning to the starting lineup against Elche . Among Mourinho's attacking decisions is whether to start Arda Güler or Yan Diomande. The coach's pre-match press conference was moved to 3:30 p.m. to accommodate the Under-20 Intercontinental Cup final at the Bernabéu.

Video: Endrick , Vinícius and Mbappé share a moment in training

There was also time for a lighter moment during the preparations, with Endrick, Vinícius Júnior and Kylian Mbappé joking with one another during the session ahead of the derby.

Julián Álvarez returns as Simeone assesses his derby options

Atlético received a fitness boost ahead of the derby, with Julián Álvarez returning to group training and being included in the squad. Pablo Barrios and Alexander Sørloth remain unavailable, while Álvarez's return gives Diego Simeone another attacking option alongside Jonathan David .

Simeone confirmed Álvarez's availability during his pre-match press conference but stopped short of revealing whether the Argentine would start.

"Julián Álvarez will be with us. We will decide whether he starts or comes on in the second half."

Discussing the tactical challenge, Simeone highlighted Madrid's ability to attack quickly after recovering possession.

"They will have a better transition than ours, more vertical… They are powerful, strong players, they play to that advantage. We have to interpret the game in the best way so that they don't feel more comfortable in their fast transitions."

The Atlético coach also expressed his admiration for Mourinho when asked about their previous encounters.

"Talking about so many years ago isn't appropriate for me. I have enormous respect for Mourinho. I admire him, and he knows how much I appreciate him. I hope we can compete like we have when we've faced each other."

For players experiencing their first Madrid derby, Simeone emphasized composure.

"I'm not one to give advice to the players who will be playing their first derby. The pressure is normal for new players. Because of the excitement a match like this generates, but stay calm. Stay calm. Football is about composure. The lads have talent. And there's one word that sums it all up: confidence."

He also placed the fixture within a busy week for the city.

"The city is having an incredible week. I was involved with Formula 1. I got to see Shakira. Now there's a derby. Madrid is growing. There's a great energy."

Returning to the match itself, Simeone said:

"A derby is different. There's enormous tension and excitement because of the rivalry, because of the competitiveness we've managed to recover in the last fifteen years. Confidence is an important quality in this match."

Víctor Muñoz reflects on his Madrid education

Víctor Muñoz has revisited his time at Real Madrid in an interview with AS, discussing the criticism he received after his Clásico appearance and the lessons he took from competing for opportunities at the club.

"These are experiences that, unfortunately, we sometimes have to go through. When it happens, as it did to me, you have to accept it and process it as best you can. In the long run, I think it's been good for me because it's made me stronger and has helped me become the footballer I am today. Everything happens for a reason."

Muñoz acknowledged that not making an appearance at the Bernabéu remained an unfulfilled ambition, while expressing appreciation for the opportunities he did receive.

"I would have loved to have made my debut at the Bernabéu, but being able to play minutes with Madrid, even if it was on other fields, was something amazing."

Asked about the difficulty of establishing himself in the first team, he said:

"I have to admit it was difficult. At first, when you're surrounded by such high-quality teammates, you realize you need to toughen up and gain experience, especially when you take a step up and join a team like Real Madrid."

Having spent time in both Barcelona's and Madrid's academies, Muñoz also outlined the different influences each had on his development.

"Both Barcelona and Real Madrid academies are impressive, and I've been able to take the best from each. As you say, at Barça I was very young, but it allowed me to learn the importance of teamwork and incorporate into my game the methodology and unique DNA they try to instill in all their youth players. At Real Madrid, it's a different style of play, more direct, and that suited my qualities very well. I'm grateful to have been at both."

Mbappé joins On in a partnership that includes an ownership stake

Kylian Mbappé has ended his long association with Nike and joined Swiss sportswear company On, which announced the partnership on Friday. The Madrid forward will become a global ambassador and work directly with the company's product teams on the development and testing of football footwear and apparel.

According to AS, citing L'Équipe , Nike had offered Mbappé a renewal worth €20 million annually over ten years. Instead, his agreement with On includes an equity stake, giving him an ownership interest in the business alongside his commercial role.

On has also appointed Thierry Henry as its director of football, while Roger Federer is already an investor in the company. The brand plans to bring its first football boots to market in 2027.

Football finance specialist Moises Assayag, quoted by AS, explained the distinction between a conventional endorsement contract and an agreement involving ownership.

"From a financial perspective, the most significant aspect of this agreement is the shift in the compensation model. When an athlete becomes a shareholder, they are no longer limited to the value of a sponsorship contract and gain direct exposure to the growth and appreciation of the company as a whole, to which they contribute their image.

"This creates a much greater alignment of interests between both parties, because the athlete's return also becomes dependent on the brand's ability to grow, generate results, and increase its market value. For a player with Mbappé's global stature, it's a strategy that transforms his own image into equity and expands the potential for long-term value creation."

The financial terms of Mbappé's On agreement, including the size of his equity stake, have not been disclosed. Its eventual value will depend partly on the company's performance and share price, rather than representing a guaranteed sponsorship payment.

articles.title: Georgia's Kirby Smart updates status of injured Nate Frazier, Isiah Canion
articles.summary: Georgia football coach Kirby Smart addresed the injuries to running back Nate Frazier and wide receiver Isiah Canion in Saturday's blowout of Arkansas.
articles.body:
FAYETEVILLE, Ark.— Georgia football lost one of its best wide receivers in the first quarter and its top running back in the third quarter Saturday in the 45-17 takedown of Arkansas.

Isiah Canion , the Georgia Tech transfer, left the game with what ABC's broadcast called a right leg injury.

Nate Frazier sustained an undisclosed injury after rushing for 75 yards on 14 carries and a touchdown.

"I think both of them are fine," coach Kirby Smart said afterwards. "I don't honstely know. Nate had a little ding. It bothered him. We're going to go check on it and Isiah the same way. I thought both of them could have played if they needed to."

Running back Chauncey Bowens had 11 carries for 39 yards and three touchdowns and running back Dwight Phillips had three catches for 20 yards.

"Interchangeable parts," Smart said. "I mean they all play, they all work, they all do the same practice habits. I like all of our backs."

Thomas Blackshear stepped up with Canion, who had three catches for 28 yards in the first two games, sidelined. He was targeted three times without a catch.

"Thomas has gotten great reps the last two weeks," Smart said. "He works really hard over there. We've got a multiple offense where multiple people can play that position. Thomas has played it well. Will Taylor has played it well."

Smart said he wished Blackshear had more targets "because he had some great routes that didn't get rewarded."

articles.title: Barcelona star sparks anger with response to boos from Sevilla fans
articles.summary: Barcelona star Lamine Yamal was at the heart of a heated exchange involving several Sevilla players during this evening’s meeting between the two clubs.This...
articles.body:
Barcelona star Lamine Yamal was at the heart of a heated exchange involving several Sevilla players during this evening's meeting between the two clubs.

This came owing to the youngster's response to harsh treatment on the part of the home crowd.

Barcelona are of course currently locked in action on the La Liga front. Fresh off six wins from six to open the defence of their crown, Hansi Flick and co. have made the trip to Andalusia to lock horns with Sevilla.

The aforementioned Lamine Yamal was in from the off for the fixture, and has since played a leading role.

articles.title: 2. Bundesliga: Former Fulham youngster Thorsteinsson extends Hertha’s perfect record
articles.summary: Hertha BSC returned to 2. Bundesliga summit with a comeback win in Dresden. Former Fulham youth team player Jón Dagur Thorsteinsson was the star of the show...
articles.body:
Hertha BSC returned to 2. Bundesliga summit with a comeback win in Dresden. Former Fulham youth team player Jón Dagur Thorsteinsson was the star of the show with his first brace in German football.

Both teams scored with their first shots on target. The hosts took the lead in the tenth minute with Patrice Čović's strike on his full 2. Bundesliga debut. The 19-year-old Werder Bremen loanee scored after playing a one-two with Vincent Vermeij .

Linus Gechter 's deflection made it difficult for Marius Gersbeck to save the effort of the former Hertha youth player. The visitors leveled the score with Nicolai Rapp nutmegged by Thorsteinsson's excellent strike.

Dresden then had their best spell of the half as Mads Pedersen and Josip Brekalo were in real danger of straight red cards. The capital city club regained momentum at the end of an action-packed half.

The league leaders had a better start to the second-half. Oluwaseun Adewumi thought he had completed the comeback with his fourth 2. Bundesliga goal, but it was disallowed by VAR for a handball.

Seconds after Christoph Daferner 's decent effort, Hertha took the lead for the first time in the evening. Thorsteinsson completed his brace with an even better long-range strike than his goal in the first-half.

The Iceland international recorded five direct goal contributions in his last four games. Instead of Dresden pushing for a late equalizer, Hertha had a couple of decent chances to extend their lead.

In the end, they held on for a 2-1 lead to maintain their perfect start to the season with their six wins out of six. Dresden entered the season's first international break in the relegation zone.

articles.title: A Coventry win 25 years in the making
articles.summary: Coventry City's win over Nottingham Forest - thanks to Jay Dasilva's goal - was a victory which was over 25 years in the making following some dark days for...
articles.body:
Hear'Say were top of the pops, a mobile phone game called 'Snake' was all the rage and Tony Blair was Prime Minister.

Wind the clock back to April 2001 and things looked rather different.

It was also the last time Coventry City tasted victory in English football's top flight.

That came courtesy of a 1-0 win over Sunderland - John Hartson heading in the winner for Gordon Strachan's side in front of 20,946 fans at Highfield Road.

Much has happened in the life of Coventry since that moment 9,287 days ago. A rollercoaster journey might be understating it.

They were relegated at the end of the 2000-01 campaign and would spend the next 11 seasons in the second tier before dropping down to League One in 2012.

Then followed a particularly dark and turbulent period in the club's history featuring points deductions and a stint in administration.

Having left Highfield Road in 2005 they became embroiled in a bitter dispute over the Ricoh Arena in 2013 and its rent.

The nadir, arguably, was when they were forced to play matches away from Coventry, at Northampton Town, before later plummeting down to the fourth tier for the first time in 59 years in 2017.

Doubtless there were those packed into the Bridgford Stand at the City Ground on Saturday who were present during those years of Sky Blue hell.

So the explosion of emotion at the full-time whistle - after Jay Dasilva 's goal settled matters - felt like Sky Blue heaven.

"It's been a tough opening for us, so those first Premier League points feel great," Coventry boss Frank Lampard told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"I thought the players were brilliant. The fight, work ethic and togetherness but also the tactical side of it. They dug and fought for each other which is what you need to win a Premier League game."

Coventry had been stranded on 99 Premier League wins for over a quarter of a century before this victory ticked them over to three figures at long last.

Lampard hopes this victory could be a key staging post in a campaign where avoiding relegation will be the main aim.

"It's really important for some of the players," he told BBC Match of the Day.

"For many of them it is their debut in the Premier League, they haven't been here before and they need to feel like they belong and play like that."

Lampard acknowledged his players must have thick skins to come through the slog of a Premier League season.

The fact this victory came off the back of a 5-0 drubbing at home to Brighton makes it all the more rewarding for the Coventry boss.

"There are lots of things we can learn and sometimes this year we may take those hits, it's a reality for teams that get to the Premier League," added Lampard.

"It's important we overcome them in terms of how we take it on board and stay together.

"It is easy to point in different directions when you lose but the group's really strong, really together, there'll have a good feeling from this one. But we'll keep our feet on the ground because it is one win, but it was needed for us."

It appeared as though the tantalizing former five-star prospect simply made too many mistakes in his first career start, with the last of those errors seemingly spoiling the second-half comeback he was orchestrating.

After all, at the time of Curtis' ill-advised throw, Vanderbilt was trailing by just three points and could have tied the game with a field goal.

Then, inexplicably, the story changed. Curtis was bailed out by another signal-caller, NC State's CJ Bailey, who also played hot potato with the game's fate in its waning moments.

While aiming to surrender a safety that would kill the clock but not cost the Wolfpack the game, Bailey lost hold of the ball in the end zone. Vanderbilt recovered and won.

articles.title: Bill Belichick, UNC vs. Dabo Swinney, Clemson Final Box Score, Top Player Stats and Highlights
articles.summary: A late offensive surge lifted Dabo Swinney and Clemson to a 28-20 victory over Bill Belichick's North Carolina at Memorial Stadium on Saturday.
articles.body:
A late offensive surge lifted Dabo Swinney and Clemson to a 28-20 victory over Bill Belichick's North Carolina at Memorial Stadium on Saturday.

The Tar Heels entered the game as a 3.5-point underdog, per FanDuel Sportsbook . They looked to be in control most of the way before giving up two fourth-quarter touchdowns to suffer their first loss of the season.

Vanderbilt gets walk-off score after brutal botch

This game, in many ways, can be split into two parts. The first was the initial 54 minutes of game time that was largely controlled by the Tar Heels. They led by as many as 14 points in the first half, thus snapping Belichick's streak of 67 straight wins with a two-touchdown advantage dating back to his NFL coaching career.

The Tar Heels led 17-15 late in the fourth quarter, but Clemson's offense wasn't getting anything going with zero touchdowns on two red-zone trips up to that point.

Nature intervened with having lightning strikes in the area, resulting in a weather delay of more than two hours that seemed to wake Clemson up.

After play resumed, North Carolina did get a field goal to go up 20-15. It could have been worse since the offense had a first-and-goal from Clemson's eight-yard line.

Clemson finally got the big play it needed on the ensuing possession with a 45-yard run by Davidson to get inside the UNC 10-yard line. He would score two plays later to give the Tigers their first lead of the game.

North Carolina's attempt to retake the lead on its next possession flamed out when Billy Edwards Jr.'s deep shot intended for Jelani Thurman on fourth-and-1 landed incomplete to give Clemson the ball back with 1:54 remaining.

Tyler Brown actually did North Carolina a favor by scoring on a 34-yard run with 1:00 left to play because it gave the Tar Heels the ball back down by eight and a chance to tie.

It didn't work out because Edwards was picked off by Elliott Washington II to end the game.

The loss will take away from a terrific effort by Hall. North Carolina's junior running back had his first career 100-yard rushing game. The Tar Heels as a team racked up 214 yards on 39 carries against Clemson's defense.

Hall, who has yet to find the end zone as a runner, caught his second touchdown pass of the season early in the game.

This was a game that served as a measuring stick of sorts for both teams. North Carolina's 2-0 record included wins over TCU and East Tennessee State.

Clemson split its first two games of the season with a blowout loss against LSU and an uninspired effort in a 22-7 victory over Georgia Southern.

Swinney's side was able to pull out the victory to get over the .500 mark. They have a short week coming up with a Friday matchup against California in Berkeley as they look to run their winning streak to three games.

The good news for Belichick is he has two weeks to get his team to regroup before they play again. The bad news is their next game is against No. 3 Notre Dame on Oct. 3.

articles.title: Dabo Swinney Reacts to Clemson's Dramatic Comeback Win vs. Bill Belichick, UNC
articles.summary: Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney heaped praise on his team following a dramatic 28-20 comeback win against Bill Belichick and North Carolina on Saturday in a game that was ultimately defined by a lengthy weather delay.
articles.body:
Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney heaped praise on his team following a dramatic 28-20 comeback win against Bill Belichick and North Carolina on Saturday in a game that was ultimately defined by a lengthy weather delay.

"Man, I just love my team," Swinney said . "They got down 17-3 and they never quit and kept battling. That's what football is. I told them, I said, 'We got eight minutes. Don't worry about anything that's happened. Let's just play this play. Let's go win second down. Let's win third down. Let's go score.' They grew up."

Clemson ultimately outscored the Tar Heels 13-3 in the fourth quarter and powered their way to a win after looking largely listless before severe weather prompted a delay midway through the fourth quarter.

True freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds, who was making his first start, went 20-of-29 for 215 yards and a touchdown.

Based on Swinney's comments, it sounds like he'll get another chance to start next Friday against Cal.

"How about this quarterback? He was pretty bad in the first half and did a couple things in the second, but what a competitor," Swinney said. "You saw a kid grow up tonight. He's going to be a problem for a long time and he ain't going to do nothing but get better."

Clemson, which opened its season with a blowout loss to LSU, has now won two games in a row and will look to move to 2-0 in conference play when it travels to Berkeley next week.

articles.body: El Racing de Ferrol resolvió con oficio y sin margen para el error uno de esos partidos de la Primera Federación que se deciden por detalles. En la jornada 4 del Grupo 1, los gallegos superaron 1-0 a un Barakaldo CF que llegó a Ferrol con la necesidad marcada en el rostro y se marchó de vacío, hundido cada vez más en la zona baja de la clasificación. El único tanto del encuentro, en el minuto 65, llevó la firma del defensa Miguel Ángel Leal, que apareció donde menos se le esperaba para desnivelar una tarde igualada. Blanco (min 84) en las filas locales y a Trigueros (min 34), Marotías (min 37), Muguruza (min 39), De la Sota (min 49) y Troncho (min 52) en las visitantes El choque, disputado el sábado 19 de septiembre a las 16:30 (CEST), tuvo un guion reconocible: un primer tiempo trabado, cargado de faltas y tarjetas, y un segundo acto en el que el Racing encontró el premio a su insistencia antes de gestionar la ventaja con la experiencia de quien sabe lo que vale un 1-0. El desarrollo: nervios primero, puntería después La primera mitad se fue sin goles y con la sensación de que el partido se jugaba más en la disputa que en las áreas. El árbitro sacó el bloc con frecuencia: por parte visitante vieron amarilla Pablo Trigueros (34'), Óscar Marotías (38') y Aritz Muguruza (40'), síntoma de un Barakaldo que optó por frenar las transiciones locales a base de faltas. Por el Racing, Germán Novoa Enríquez fue amonestado en el 42'. Con ese cúmulo de interrupciones, el 0-0 al descanso hizo justicia a un tramo sin claridad. El técnico del Barakaldo movió ficha ya en el reinicio, con la entrada de Sergio Camus por Aritz Muguruza (46'), y volvió a retocar en el 61' con el doble cambio de Xabier Sola y Markel Ruiz por Ager Badiola y Endika Mateos Bezana, buscando otra energía arriba. Pero el que golpeó fue el local. En el minuto 65, Álvaro Ramón puso el centro y Miguel Ángel Leal lo transformó en el 1-0 que ya no se movería. Un defensa central resolviendo lo que los delanteros no habían podido: la esencia del fútbol de urgencias. A partir de ahí, el Racing administró. El cuerpo técnico ferrolano refrescó el once con las entradas de Unai Ropero y Raúl Blanco (70'), Etienne Eto'o Pineda y Vicente Esquerdo (78') y Saúl García (88'), gestión de minutos y de piernas frescas para cerrar espacios. El Barakaldo lo intentó con los cambios de Álvaro Peña y Urko Collado (73'), pero le faltó pegada: llegó a Ferrol con solo dos goles a favor en cuatro jornadas, y esa falta de gol volvió a condenarlo. Los protagonistas El nombre de la tarde fue Miguel Ángel Leal, central que firmó el gol decisivo y confirmó que el Racing tiene salida de balón y llegada desde su línea defensiva. La asistencia corrió a cargo de Álvaro Ramón, lateral titular que aportó el desborde y el centro justo antes de ser sustituido en el tramo final. En el capitán Fabio González el conjunto verdiblanco tuvo el orden en el centro del campo, con el veterano Daniel Ojeda aportando criterio hasta su relevo. Enfrente, el Barakaldo se aferró a la figura de su portero Gaizka Campos y de su capitán Julen Huidobro Betolaza, pero el bloque fabril de Ferrol y la falta de acierto en el último pase impidieron cualquier reacción. El acumular de amonestaciones tempranas también condicionó la propuesta visitante, obligada a medir cada entrada durante buena parte del encuentro. Lo que dice la clasificación El triunfo mantiene al Racing de Ferrol en la zona noble del Grupo 1: con la victoria, los gallegos suman 7 puntos (2 victorias, 1 empate, 1 derrota en cuatro jornadas) y se instalan en la octava posición dentro de un pelotón apretadísimo. Nada menos que siete equipos comparten esos 7 puntos, con la diferencia de goles como único juez: por encima del Racing aparecen, entre otros, el Real Unión Club, el filial del Athletic Club, el CD Lugo, el Mirandés, el Pontevedra CF y el CP Cacereño. En lo más alto manda la UD Logroñés con 10 puntos, invicta tras tres victorias y un empate. Para el Racing, la lectura es doble: la victoria le permite no descolgarse del vagón de cabeza, pero la exigüidad del marcador y su +1 de diferencia de goles le obligan a afinar la puntería si quiere escalar posiciones en un grupo donde cada gol pesa. El Barakaldo, en zona de alarma El panorama es bien distinto para el Barakaldo CF, que sigue con 4 puntos (1 victoria, 1 empate, 2 derrotas) y ocupa la decimoquinta plaza con una diferencia de goles de -3, la más pobre del tramo medio-bajo entre los conjuntos con puntuación similar. Solo dos tantos marcados en cuatro jornadas dibujan el problema de fondo: al equipo vasco le cuesta horrores generar peligro, y esa sequía lo empuja hacia una parte baja que ya asoma amenazante, con el Arenas Club y la Unión Deportiva Ourense —esta última aún sin puntuar— cerrando la tabla. La derrota en A Malata no es dramática por sí sola, pero encadena señales preocupantes. Si el Barakaldo no encuentra pronto vías de gol, la temporada puede convertirse muy rápido en una lucha por la permanencia. Conclusión El Racing de Ferrol ganó como ganan los equipos que aspiran a estar arriba: sin brillar, pero sin conceder, y resolviendo el partido con un jugador poco habitual en el casillero de goleadores. Miguel Ángel Leal y Álvaro Ramón combinaron el instante decisivo de una tarde marcada por la tensión. El Barakaldo, en cambio, se marcha de Galicia con las mismas dudas con las que llegó y una necesidad cada vez más urgente: marcar goles. En la Primera Federación, donde los puntos se reparten con cuentagotas, ese 1-0 vale mucho más de lo que aparenta.

articles.title: El Teruel sigue sin marcar tras cuatro partidos
articles.standfirst: El conjunto aragonés resistió bien hasta la segunda parte, pero claudicó por culpa de sus propios errores y enlaza la tercera derrota seguida
articles.summary: El conjunto aragonés resistió bien hasta la segunda parte, pero claudicó por culpa de sus propios errores y enlaza la tercera derrota seguida
articles.body: El Rayo Majadahonda encontró en la segunda parte el desahogo que su arranque de temporada reclamaba. Con dos golpes certeros tras el descanso —obra de Manin Gonzaga y José Cambra— los madrileños derrotaron por 2-0 a un CD Teruel que se hunde en el vagón de cola del Grupo 2 y que, cuatro jornadas después, todavía no ha visto puerta esta campaña. El resultado empuja al conjunto local hasta los 4 puntos y le permite tomar aire, mientras el Teruel se queda anclado en la parte baja con un solo punto y un balance ofensivo alarmante. FICHA TÉCNICA Rayo Majadahonda: Prieto; Diez (Choco, min 65'), Ramos, Sina, Mesa (Durán, min 84'); Tarsi, Quintanilla (Del Pozo, min 65'); Yoshimura (Celorio, min 77'), Cambra (Ramos, min 77'), Raúl Hernández; Manín. C.D. Teruel: Amador Zarco; Borge (Goyo, min 84'), Relu, Álvaro López, Pablo Felipe (Borikó, min 70'), Joserra; Romera (Belevonis, min 70'), Albisua (Redón, min 57'); Mario Sesé, Gallardo; Moraitis (Sergio Moreno, min 57'). Árbitro: Javier Figueiredo Comesaña. Amonestó a Diez (min 11'), Albisua (min 26'), Gallardo (min 41'). Goles: 1-0, Manín (min 53'), 2-0, Cambra (min 75'). Incidencias: Partido correspondiente a la cuarta jornada del grupo 2 de Primera RFEF disputado en el estadio Cerro del Espino (Majadahonda). Un primer tiempo trabado, resuelto en la reanudación El acta del encuentro refleja un primer acto sin goles (0-0 al descanso) y con más nerviosismo que fútbol. Las tarjetas marcaron el ritmo: amonestación local en el minuto 12 y dos avisos visitantes antes del intermedio, a Haritz Albisua (27') y a Edu Gallardo (42'), síntoma de un Teruel obligado a frenar por la vía de la falta. Todo cambió al reanudarse el juego. En el minuto 53, Manin Gonzaga culminó una jugada asistida por Alejandro Díez Salomón para abrir el marcador y romper el guion de tablas. El delantero, uno de los hombres de mayor peso ofensivo en el once de Majadahonda, firmó el 1-0 que encarriló la tarde. El Teruel reaccionó de inmediato en el banquillo: en el 57' entraron Hugo Redón y Sergio Moreno por Albisua y Panagiotis Moraitis, buscando frescura y presencia arriba. Pero el plan no fructificó. El propio Majadahonda administró el partido, dio entrada a Choco y David Del Pozo en el 65' y, diez minutos después, sentenció. En el minuto 75, José Cambra recogió una asistencia de Raúl Hernández para establecer el 2-0 definitivo. Con el partido resuelto, el técnico local movió el banquillo con Iñigo Ramos Gálvez, Neco Celorio y Juan Durán, mientras el Teruel agotaba sus cambios con Christos Belevonis, Santi Borikó y Goyo Medina sin lograr acortar distancias. El acta cerró en 2-0 al pitido final. Los protagonistas Manin Gonzaga fue el desnivelador. Su gol en el 53' desatascó un choque encallado y confirmó su condición de referencia arriba para el conjunto madrileño, que salió al campo con un 4-2-3-1 pensado precisamente para alimentar al ariete. José Cambra, partiendo desde la mediapunta, redondeó la tarde con el segundo tanto y dejó su firma en un partido clave para las aspiraciones locales. Mención especial para Raúl Hernández y Alejandro Díez Salomón, los dos repartidores de asistencias. El lateral Díez Salomón, además de habilitar el primer gol, fue de los más activos antes de ser relevado por Choco en el 65'. En el Teruel, el griego Panagiotis Moraitis —el futbolista de mayor valoración de mercado del once visitante— apenas pudo influir y fue sustituido en el 57'. La pólvora mojada de los aragoneses volvió a ser el gran lastre. Lo que dice la clasificación El triunfo tiene lectura inmediata en la tabla del Grupo 2. El Rayo Majadahonda, que llegaba con un balance de 1 victoria, 1 empate y 2 derrotas, escala hasta los 4 puntos y se sitúa en la 12ª posición, dejando atrás la zona más comprometida. Con 5 goles a favor y 5 en contra, equilibra su diferencia de goles y afronta las próximas jornadas con una base sobre la que construir. En lo alto del grupo, el pulso lo mantienen el Villarreal B U23 y el Real Jaén, ambos con 10 puntos, seguidos de cerca por el Real Murcia (9) y el Atlético Madrileño (8). El Majadahonda queda todavía lejos de esa pelea, pero el margen sobre el descenso empieza a ser su prioridad. El Teruel, en zona de máxima alarma El panorama para el CD Teruel es preocupante. Tras cuatro jornadas, el cuadro aragonés ocupa la 19ª plaza con un solo punto (0 victorias, 1 empate, 3 derrotas). Pero el dato que enciende todas las alarmas es su registro goleador: cero goles a favor y siete en contra, la peor cifra ofensiva del grupo y una diferencia de -7 que solo mejora ligeramente al Algeciras CF, colista con cero puntos. El equipo suma ya tres derrotas y sigue sin ser capaz de generar peligro sostenido. La falta de gol se ha convertido en una losa que condiciona cada partido: sin marcar, cualquier concesión defensiva se traduce en derrota. La visita a Majadahonda solo confirmó una tendencia que el técnico visitante deberá corregir con urgencia si no quiere ver cómo el pelotón se aleja definitivamente. Conclusión El 2-0 fue justo por lo visto sobre el césped: un Majadahonda paciente que supo esperar su momento y ejecutar con eficacia en cuanto encontró grietas, y un Teruel voluntarioso pero inofensivo. Gonzaga y Cambra pusieron los goles; Díez Salomón y Raúl Hernández, las asistencias. Para los locales, tres puntos de oxígeno. Para los aragoneses, otra jornada sin recompensa y la sensación creciente de que la salvación pasa, antes que nada, por reencontrarse con el gol.

articles.summary: The Louisville Cardinals were Saturday's early winner in the College Football Playoff perspective.
articles.body:
The Louisville Cardinals were Saturday's early winner in the College Football Playoff perspective.

Louisville picked up a win over the SMU Mustangs in the marquee game of the mid-afternoon slate.

The Cardinals should now be viewed as the No. 1 contender to the Miami Hurricanes in the ACC.

The Texas A&M Aggies suffered Saturday's biggest set back so far. They fell at home to the Kentucky Wildcats.

A&M's playoff hopes aren't completely dashed, but the early defeat at the start of a tough SEC schedule is a big step backwards for the Aggies.

Saturday's biggest game takes place in primetime, as Lane Kiffin and the LSU Tigers visit the Ole Miss Rebels in a battle of top-10 programs in Oxford.

Texas A&M Suffers Upset Loss To Kentucky

Texas A&M opened SEC play with a surprising home loss at the hands of Kentucky.

Aggies quarterback Marcel Reed threw a pair of picks in the loss. A&M was down three touchdowns by the end of the third quarter.

Mike Elko's team fell short in its come-from-behind effort and suffered its first defeat of the campaign.

The season obviously isn't over for the Aggies with the 12-team playoff format, but the early loss puts them in a difficult spot, especially with their SEC schedule.

A&M still has to go on the road at Missouri, Alabama and Oklahoma and it plays Tennessee at home.

The margin for error is very slim now for A&M, who will likely drop out of the top 15 in Sunday's AP Top 25.

However, if the Aggies pull off a handful of ranked wins in league play, they could still get in as an at-large team.

Louisville Takes Big Step With ACC Win Over SMU

Louisville took a big step in its playoff contention with a home win over SMU.

SMU and Louisville entered the weekend as the presumed No. 2 and No. 3 in the ACC behind Miami.

Louisville now has a leg up on SMU in the race to get to the ACC Championship Game, where it will likely face Miami, who seems to be a class above everyone else in the conference.

The Cardinals entered Saturday at No. 23 in the AP Top 25, so they won't be in the projected playoff positions yet, but Saturday was a good first step toward a potential at-large, or even an ACC automatic berth.

Louisville doesn't play Miami in the regular season, so now that it has no more ranked teams on its schedule, it should continue to climb in the rankings.

The Cardinals are 2-1 because they lost to Ole Miss in Week 1, but that loss might not matter much in the 12-team playoff era when multiple losses can get a team into the field.

articles.body: Valencia y Real Sociedad se enfrentan esta noche en Mestalla (21.00) con el objetivo de lograr un resultado que les permita ir al parón con cierta calma. Tras la victoria en Mendizorroza, el equipo blanquinegro ha frenado la caída, pero no eliminado sus urgencias. El conjunto txuriurdin comparece con la ambición de reaccionar tras haber vuelto a caer en un valle de resultados. Será un día especial para Óscar Sánchez, técnico del filial que se despide del primer equipo en su campo. El club espera presentar la próxima semana a Aguirre como nuevo entrenador. En el apartado deportivo, Óscar Sánchez confirmó que dispone de todos los futbolistas que viajaron a Vitoria y avanzó que repetirá la convocatoria para recibir a la Real Sociedad. La principal novedad es la recuperación de Luis Rioja, que completó el último entrenamiento pese a las molestias que arrastraba y está en condiciones de entrar en la lista. El técnico también dejó la puerta abierta a seguir contando con el canterano Aarón Mayol tras su reciente irrupción. Si hay algo en Mestalla, es ganas de celebrar. Y estaría bien empezar por un gol. El Valencia no ha marcado ningún tanto en sus tres primeros partidos como local, algo que no había sucedido nunca. La Real Sociedad, por su parte, visita Mestalla después de sufrir dos derrotas seguidas de local que le han hecho mucho daño, sobre todo la de este pasado jueves frente al Bournemouth, porque al flojo estado de forma de algunos futbolistas importantes, como Kubo, el propio Oyarzabal, Guedes o Soler, se ha añadido el debate en la portería, donde Pellegrino Matarazzo está alternando a Remiro y Marrero, y las dudas sobre las capacidades del propio entrenador. El de Nueva Jersey, que parece que volverá a tirar de Remiro, recupera para su defensa al sancionado el jueves Aramburu, que será titular junto a Jon Martín, Sarr y Sergio Gómez. Las novedades apuntan a llegar de medio campo para adelante, ya que Soler acompañará en su regreso a casa a Yangel Herrera o Gorrotxategi en el doble pivote, y el exblanquinegro Guedes también volvería en un ataque nuevo.Y es que desde el banquillo podrían entrar también Kubo y Sucic, los tres por detrás de Mikel Oyarzabal, que esta vez sería el delantero.

articles.body: Deportivo de La Coruña y Real Betis Balompié se enfrentan hoy domingo 20 de septiembre desde las 18.30 horas en el Estadio de Riazor en partido correspondiente a la séptima jornada de LaLiga EA Sports. Será el último encuentro para ambos conjuntos antes de la primera fecha FIFA de selecciones de la temporada, importante para despedir este tramo inicial de la competición doméstica con tres puntos más en el camino hacia sus objetivos. El Deportivo afronta el encuentro después de sufrir el miércoles, frente al Sevilla su primera derrota del curso. Antonio Hidalgo tendrá que gestionar el cansancio de un equipo que disputará su tercer encuentro en siete días y, además, está pendiente de varios futbolistas afectados por un proceso vírico. "Físicamente estamos intentando recuperar a la gente de la mejor manera posible. A eso se nos ha añadido un proceso vírico en algunos jugadores. Vamos a ver cómo van evolucionando de cara al partido", explicó el técnico. Los coruñeses han sumado dos victorias, tres empates y una derrota en su regreso a Primera. El Betis llega a Riazor en plena racha después de ganar sus cuatro últimos partidos oficiales, frente al Real Madrid, Lille (en la Champions), Villarreal y Getafe. Los de Manuel Pellegrini son terceros, igualados a 15 puntos con el Real Madrid, y han ganado cinco de sus seis encuentros de Liga. articles.body: El sensacional regreso del Deportivo de La Coruña a Primera división, sin conocer la derrota en las cinco primeras jornadas y con dos victorias de prestigio, ante Valencia y Villarreal, recibió el pasado miércoles su primer varapalo.
